label: Nature Biotechnology
description: Nature Biotechnology (Nature Portfolio / Springer Nature), the pipeline's default venue. Every number in this profile is quoted from the journal's own public author pages, retrieved 2026-10-01: the Content Types page (https://www.nature.com/nbt/content) states Article abstract <= 150 words and main text <= 3,000 words excluding abstract, Methods, references and figure legends, Brief Communication abstract <= 70 words (3 sentences) with 1,000-1,500 words of main text including abstract, references and figure legends, Resource abstract 100-150 words with main text <= 3,000 words, Review 3,000-4,000 words, Perspective <= 3,000 words, Correspondence 300-800 words and Feature <= 3,000 words; the specialist Matters Arising page states 'ideally not exceed 1,200 words'. A type the page gives no number for (Analysis, Comment, News & Views, Book Review, Patent Article, Careers and Recruitment, Primer) carries null, so the stages count the section and name the venue's own table instead of borrowing the Article caps. The Article limits (150/3,000) keep the +10%/+25% margins the pipeline was originally written with (promoted caps 165/3,750); every other type is applied with no margin (relaxation 1.0).

article_types.label: Article
article_types.source: https://www.nature.com/nbt/content (checked 2026-10-01), 'Article': 'An Article is a substantial novel research study, with a complex story often involving several techniques or approaches.' Format: 'Main text - up to 3,000 words, excluding abstract, Methods, references and figure legends. Abstract - up to 150 words, unreferenced. Display items - up to 6 items (figures and/or tables).' The same entry prescribes the section order 'Introduction (without heading), Results, Discussion, Online Methods' and recommends up to 50 references, none of which this profile models.

length_limits.source: https://www.nature.com/nbt/content (checked 2026-10-01), Article format: abstract <= 150 words, unreferenced; main text <= 3,000 words excluding abstract, Methods, references and figure legends

abstract.note: https://www.nature.com/nbt/content (checked 2026-10-01), 'Article' format: 'Abstract - up to 150 words, unreferenced.' The +10% relaxation is this pipeline's own margin (the one the shipped profile carried before this verification), not an NBT rule; the promoted cap is 165 words.

main_text.note: https://www.nature.com/nbt/content (checked 2026-10-01), 'Article' format: 'Main text - up to 3,000 words, excluding abstract, Methods, references and figure legends.' The +25% relaxation is this pipeline's own margin (unchanged from the rule set the pipeline shipped with), not an NBT rule; the promoted cap is 3,750 words. The same page caps display items at 6 (figures and/or tables) and recommends up to 50 references -- neither is modelled here.

cover_letter.source: master-prompt preference (300-500 words in the persuading part). Nature Biotechnology states no cover-letter word limit; its Preparing your material page (https://www.nature.com/nbt/submission-guidelines/preparing-your-submission, checked 2026-10-01) says only that 'The cover letter should explain the importance of the work, and why you consider it appropriate for the diverse readership of Nature Biotechnology', that it should disclose related manuscripts, prior editorial discussions and (for double-anonymized peer review) author affiliations, and that it is not seen by peer reviewers. The 650-word total_max is the operator's own TOTAL-content cap (salutation, body, disclosures and signature), not an NBT rule.

captions.source: https://www.nature.com/nbt/submission-guidelines/aip-and-formatting (checked 2026-10-01), 'Figure legends': 'Ensure the legend does not exceed the word limit of the article type.' Nature Biotechnology publishes no separate legend word count, so published_limit is null and the pipeline counts legends without a cap.

main_text.note: https://www.nature.com/nbt/content (checked 2026-10-01), 'Brief Communication' format: 'Main text - 1,000-1,500 words, including abstract, references and figure legends, and contains no headings.' article_types.label: Comment
article_types.source: https://www.nature.com/nbt/content (checked 2026-10-01), 'Comment': 'A Comment is a flexible format that focuses on the scientific, commercial, ethical, legal, societal, or political issues surrounding research.'

length_limits.source: https://www.nature.com/nbt/content (checked 2026-10-01), Comment format: 'Length - typically 1-4 pages, although some may be longer. There are no specific structural guidelines.'

abstract.note: https://www.nature.com/nbt/content (checked 2026-10-01), 'Comment' format, states no abstract and no abstract word count; base and relaxation are null (no number invented).

main_text.note: https://www.nature.com/nbt/content (checked 2026-10-01), 'Comment' format gives a PAGE range ('typically 1-4 pages, although some may be longer'), not a word count, so base and relaxation are null; a page limit is not a word count and this schema does not model it. The same entry says references should be used sparingly, up to 15, and that Comments 'do not normally contain primary research data'.

article_types.label: Matters Arising
article_types.source: https://www.nature.com/nbt/submission-guidelines/matters-arising (checked 2026-10-01): 'Matters Arising are exceptionally interesting and timely scientific comments and clarifications on original research papers published in Nature Biotechnology.'

length_limits.source: https://www.nature.com/nbt/submission-guidelines/matters-arising (checked 2026-10-01): 'The main text should be as concise as possible, and ideally not exceed 1,200 words. Any extended Methods may be reported as Supplementary Information.'

abstract.note: https://www.nature.com/nbt/submission-guidelines/matters-arising (checked 2026-10-01) publishes no abstract word count: it says only that 'Contributions should start with a brief paragraph that summarizes the message of the article without specialized terminology, for a non-specialist readership. This paragraph should be used as the abstract for submission purposes.' base and relaxation are null (no number invented).

main_text.note: https://www.nature.com/nbt/submission-guidelines/matters-arising (checked 2026-10-01): 'The main text should be as concise as possible, and ideally not exceed 1,200 words.' The venue states this as an ideal ceiling, so the profile applies the number with no margin (relaxation 1.0); the same page's guideline of up to 15 references is not modelled.

The page marks Features (with Comment, News & Views, Book Review, Patent Article, Careers and Recruitment, Primer and Correspondence) as non-primary content that is not eligible for Open Access.

length_limits.source: https://www.nature.com/nbt/content (checked 2026-10-01), Feature format: 'Length - up to 3,000 words. Use of tables and figures is strongly encouraged. Written in a journalistic style, accessible to a wide range of non-specialist readers.'

Note this is a non-primary, journalistic content type (see the same page's footnote), not a research manuscript; the review and rewrite models assume a research package and will report most checks as not applicable.

tables.source: Nature Biotechnology formatting guide, '2 - Tables' (https://www.nature.com/nbt/for-authors/formatting-guide, checked 2026-10-04): 'Please include tables at the end of your text document. Complex tables can be submitted as a separate Excel file.' The guide does not state which side of a table carries its title/legend, so the caption side follows established academic convention (level 3 of this pipeline's fallback chain): a table's own title/legend sits immediately before the table.
tables.note: This venue declares NO special table: every table of the main text follows the rule (the guide's own exception -- a complex table shipped as a separate Excel file -- is a separate FILE, not a differently shaped table in the manuscript).
tables.caption: before

submission.pdf_note: Nature Biotechnology accepts a PDF for the INITIAL submission -- 'We accept initial submissions in PDF, Word or TeX/LaTeX formats; if you are using TeX/LaTeX, please submit compiled PDFs' (https://www.nature.com/nbt/submission-guidelines/initial-formatting, checked 2026-10-01) -- so a reader or editor may open exactly that PDF. The accepted version must be Word or TeX/LaTeX: 'Please submit your manuscript in either Word or TeX/LaTeX format. We do not accept PDFs for final submissions' (https://www.nature.com/nbt/submission-guidelines/aip-and-formatting, checked 2026-10-01).
submission.initial_submission_note: https://www.nature.com/nbt/submission-guidelines/initial-formatting (checked 2026-10-01): 'Your initial submission does not need to be specially formatted, as long as the study is described in a way that is suitable for editorial assessment and peer review.'
submission.latex_note: https://www.nature.com/nbt/submission-guidelines/aip-and-formatting (checked 2026-10-01): 'To submit a TeX/LaTeX file, please use any of the standard class files such as article.cls, revtex.cls or amsart.cls', and 'For further guidelines on TeX/LaTeX, please visit https://www.springernature.com/gp/authors/campaigns/latex-author-support where you can download the Springer Nature LaTeX template.' A copy of that template is staged in nature-biotechnology.official/.
